title: In ovo injection corticosterone method for physiological and behavioral studies in chickens
author: Ahmed, Essa

steps.title: Prepare corticosterone solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve corticosterone (CORT) in absolute alcohol, then dilute with phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) to obtain two solutions delivering 0.2 µg (low dose) or 1 µg (high dose) of CORT in a total volume of 100 µL, ensuring the final mixture contains only a minimal amount of alcohol.

steps.title: Allocate eggs to treatment groups
steps.instruction: Collect fertilized eggs laid by hens one month after onset of lay and randomly assign them to three groups: PBS control, low‑dose CORT (0.2 µg), and high‑dose CORT (1 µg).

steps.title: Aseptic washing of eggs
steps.instruction: Prior to incubation, wash each egg with alcohol to provide aseptic conditions.

steps.title: In‑ovo injection
steps.instruction: Under aseptic conditions, inject 100 µL of the appropriate solution (PBS, low‑dose, or high‑dose) into each egg using a Hamilton syringe. Create a hole in the middle of the long axis of the egg, advance the needle approximately 20 mm below the surface until the yolk membrane is penetrated, then deliver the volume. Randomize injection order across groups.

steps.title: Incubate eggs (first experiment)
steps.instruction: Place the injected eggs in a forced‑draught incubator set to 37.5 ± 0.3 °C with 55 %–57 % relative humidity. Program automatic turning every two hours. Incubate until hatching.

steps.title: Incubate eggs (second experiment – pre‑injection)
steps.instruction: For the second experiment, incubate eggs under the same conditions for 10 days before injection.

steps.title: Second‑round injection and continued incubation
steps.instruction: After 10 days, remove eggs, inject the same 100 µL solutions (PBS, 0.2 µg, or 1 µg CORT) as described in the In‑ovo injection step, then return eggs to the incubator and continue incubation under the same temperature and humidity settings until hatching.

steps.title: Post‑hatch drying
steps.instruction: Allow chicks to remain in the incubator for approximately 12 hours after hatching to dry completely before removal.

steps.title: Initial chick processing
steps.instruction: At one day of age, weigh each chick, apply a wing label, and transfer chicks to battery cages illuminated with constant fluorescent light.

steps.title: First‑week rearing environment
steps.instruction: Maintain room temperature at 32–35 °C during the first week, then decrease temperature by 3 °C each subsequent week until reaching 21 °C. Keep relative humidity between 40 % and 60 %.

steps.title: Transfer to floor pens and husbandry
steps.instruction: After the first week, move both sexes to floor pens with sawdust litter, maintain a stock density of 20–25 kg m⁻², and continue lighting, ventilation, feeding, and management in accordance with the Feeding Management Regulations of Yellow‑feathered Chicken (NY/T 1871‑2010).
